what_its_for: Cefuroxime axetil is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections. It is commonly prescribed for ear infections, sinus infections, throat infections (like strep throat), urinary tract infections (UTIs), skin infections, bronchitis, pneumonia, and Lyme disease. It only works against bacteria — it will NOT treat viral infections like the common cold or flu.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth exactly as your doctor prescribed. Tablets should be swallowed whole or crushed and mixed with a small amount of food if you have trouble swallowing. It is very important to take cefuroxime WITH FOOD — this helps your body absorb the medicine better and reduces stomach upset. The oral suspension (liquid) for children should be shaken well before each use and taken with food as well. Always finish your entire prescription, even if you start feeling better. Stopping early can allow the infection to come back and may make it harder to treat.
dosing: Your dose will depend on the type and severity of your infection, your age, and your kidney function. Common adult doses range from 250 mg to 500 mg taken twice a day (every 12 hours). Children's doses are based on weight and are usually given twice a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not take more or less than what is prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep them away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. The liquid suspension should be stored in the refrigerator and used within 10 days. Shake it well before each use. Dispose of any unused liquid after 10 days. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium at the same time as this medicine, as they may reduce how well the drug is absorbed. Avoid alcohol while taking this antibiotic, as it can increase the risk of side effects. Do not take this medicine if you have had a serious allergic reaction (such as hives, swelling, or difficulty breathing) to cefuroxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics, or penicillin antibiotics — tell your doctor right away. Do not share this medicine with others, even if they have similar symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency help right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing or swallowing); severe diarrhea or diarrhea with blood or mucus (this could be a serious gut infection called C. difficile); yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or unusual fatigue (possible liver problems); seizures; severe stomach pain or cramping; or if your symptoms are not improving after a few days of treatment or if they get worse.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting this antibiotic. However, it is very important to complete the full course of treatment as prescribed, even if you feel well before finishing. The full course is usually 5 to 14 days depending on your infection type. If you do not feel any improvement after 3 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney disease. Make sure to tell your doctor about any kidney problems before starting this medicine. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Cefuroxime is generally considered safe during pregnancy when needed, but always let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Small amounts can pass into breast milk. Elderly patients: Older adults may need a lower dose, especially if kidney function is reduced. Children: The liquid suspension is available for children who cannot swallow tablets. Dosing is based on the child's weight. Allergy history: If you are allergic to penicillin, tell your doctor — there is a small chance you may also react to cefuroxime. Your doctor will decide if this medicine is still safe for you.
